title: Slice prioritization and fallback lab notes
content:
Context:
This is a working lab doc to capture experiments, heuristics, and failure-mode playbooks for breaking down rollout traffic into prioritized slices and for defining robust fallback behavior when a slice experiences degradation. Intended audience: product PMs, rollout owners, SREs, and solutions engineers.

Goals:
- Give a concrete, reproducible pattern for prioritizing user traffic by risk, feature-value, and cost sensitivity.
- Define deterministic fallback behaviors that are safe for customer experience and predictable for billing/latency.
- Surface a compact set of metrics and thresholds that cross-functional teams can agree on without long bespoke analysis.

Non-goals:
- This document does not aim to replace fine-grained safety review for ML outputs (that belongs to the safety/ops team).
- Not an exhaustive A/B statistics primer; see linked artifacts for stat-testing defaults.

Quick summary of approach:
1) Partition users into slices using a 3-axis prioritization: business-criticality (high/med/low), feature-importance (core/adjunct/experimental), and latency-sensitivity (hot/warm/cold).
2) Assign an ordinal priority score and map to traffic percentages per phase (phase 0 -> 100% internal, phase 1 -> 1%, phase 2 -> 5%, phase 3 -> 25%, phase 4 -> 100%).
3) Attach a lightweight rollback/fallback policy to each slice: immediate fallback to baseline model, degraded feature toggle, or queued processing depending on latency and correctness signals.

Slicing rules (practical):
- Business-criticality: derived from contract SLAs / revenue impact tags. Example: billing API calls = high; social feed personalization = medium; experimental assistant widget = low.
- Feature-importance: whether the new change modifies the API surface or only internal scoring. API-breaking or deterministic changes are treated strictly.
- Latency-sensitivity: route classification from opt-in telemetry (end-to-end p95 latency bucket).

Concrete slice naming convention (short codes):
- HC-CORE-HOT (High business, core feature, latency sensitive)
- MC-ADJ-WARM
- LC-EXP-COLD
Use short codes to make dashboards and alert rules compact.

Priority scoring (example):
- HC-CORE-HOT = 100
- HC-CORE-WARM = 90
- MC-ADJ-HOT = 70
- LC-EXP-COLD = 20
Sort descending to allocate traffic first to highest scoring slices during phased ramp.

Traffic allocation template by phase (suggested):
- Phase 0 (internal dogfood): 0.1% (internal only), smoke tests, QA gates
- Phase 1 (pilot): 1% to HC slices only for 24 hours
- Phase 2 (broader pilot): 5% including HC and MC core slices for 48–72 hours
- Phase 3 (public beta): 25% including adjoint medium slices for 7 days
- Phase 4 (general availability): 100%
Notes: times and percentages are knobs—use traffic intensity to control risk.

Metric set (minimal, cross-functional):
- Safety: %responses flagged by safety classifier (rolling 1h and 24h windows)
- Correctness: regression delta on golden prompts (avg token-level score)
- Latency: p50/p95 end-to-end (client-perceived) and model-server p95
- Error rate: 5xxs, timeouts (> model timeout threshold), and soft-fails (partial outputs)
- Business signal: conversion rate / API success rate for HC slices
Define dashboards using these 6 panels across rows per slice.

Automated gating rules (ops-safe defaults):
- Immediate rollback condition: safety > 0.5% absolute increase AND business metric degradation > 1.5x baseline over 30m
- Degraded-mode trigger: p95 latency > SLA target + 200ms for sustained 10m -> route slice to degraded flow (shorter context / cached responses)
- Escalation: error-rate spike (2x baseline in 5m) -> page on-call SRE and remove slice from rollout (auto-rollback)
Example threshold numbers are intentionally conservative; teams should calibrate per product line.

Fallback options (ordered by severity):
1) Soft degrade: reduce model context/turn off non-essential plugins and keep flow online.
2) Model fallback: route to last-known-good model (smaller/cheaper quantized variant)
3) Feature toggle: disable the new surfaced UI (server-side toggle) and return stable experience
4) Queue + async: accept request and respond with a placeholder, process asynchronously, send update via webhook (only for non-interactive flows)
5) Full rollback: re-route 100% of slice to baseline model/version and hold rollout

Decision rules for which fallback to use:
- If latency-only (no safety or correctness regression) -> prefer soft degrade or model fallback.
- If safety regression detected -> immediate model fallback or full rollback depending on severity.
- If business metric shows conversion hit but no safety issues -> consider feature toggle while triaging.

Operational runbook (short):
- Owner (phase): the PM running the rollout and an SRE on-call assigned as rollout buddy.
- Monitoring: enable slice-specific dashboards before enabling any traffic; hook anomaly detection (rolling Z-score) with 1m granularity for p95 and error rate.
- Escalation flow: on-call paged -> SRE runs quick-check checklist (is model overloaded? Is upstream database slow? Is there a config drift?) -> apply fastest safe fallback -> notify stakeholders in #rollouts channel with initial findings.
- Postmortem: if rollback occurs, capture timeline, root cause, and mitigations in RNFD-XXXX (Jira).

Sample quick-check checklist for SRE (copy-paste):
- Is the target shard overloaded? (kubectl top, gpu metrics)
- Is QPS distribution abnormal for the slice? (per-slice QPS panels)
- Any infra alerts (disk, network)? (PagerDuty -> infra alerts)
- Any abnormal model logs (OOMs, slow kernels)? (log tail)
- If nothing infra, then revert to model fallback or toggle off new feature

Example SQL for measuring conversion delta (placeholder):
SELECT
  slice_code,
  count(*) as requests,
  avg(case when event = 'conversion' then 1 else 0 end) as conv_rate
FROM events
WHERE team = 'assistant'
  AND timestamp >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY slice_code;

A/B testing notes (quick):
- For experiments that alter surface-level responses (copy tone, structure), run paired evaluations against canonical prompts (at least 300 prompts in the golden set).
- Use sequential testing with predefined stopping rules, but default to fixed-horizon 7-day windows for most rollout-driven experiments to avoid peeking bias.
- Prefer stratified sampling by slice to preserve risk partitioning.

Ceremony and comms (recommended):
- Pre-roll checklist: owner, SLOs defined, dashboards live, rollback plan documented, stakeholders tagged.
- Kickoff: Slack thread + short 15min sync with PM, rollout buddy SRE, and prod lead.
- Mid-roll ping: 1h and 6h standups during pilot phases, daily during public beta.
- Close: short retro and decision memo published to Confluence.

Open questions / experiments to try:
- Adaptive slice scaling: can we automatically expand a slice’s traffic when model latency headroom > 20% and safety metrics stable? (experiment idea)
- Dynamic fallback selection: given multiple fallback paths, can we learn which fallback minimizes business impact based on historical incidents? (requires instrumentation)
- Cost-aware rollouts: include estimated cost delta per-slice in rollout UI to help PMs make tradeoffs.

Next immediate steps (action items):
- [Aisha] Draft a lightweight dashboard template and share in #rollouts by 2026-03-05
- [Liam] Prototype slice allocation control in canary-routing service (PR link in linked artifacts) by 2026-03-12
- [María] Run a dry-run with internal traffic using HC-CORE-HOT slice next week and report safety metric baseline

Notes-to-self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Keep slice IDs short. Avoid mixing too many dimensions in the UI, show 1 primary and 1 secondary attribute.
- We should persist slice assignments for users with sticky sessions to avoid flapping when traffic allocation changes.
- Need a tiny cost-estimation panel: tokens/sec * model-cost-per-token -> helps when deciding whether MC slices should be expanded.
